subject: general
question: ​A person with 30 km/h reaches Dharmatala to Eden Garden in 30 minutes. If he has to reach the distance in 20 minutes, then what will be his speed (in km/h) ?
solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the person = 30 km/h

He travels the distance in 30 minutes.

But he has to cover the distance in 20 minutes.

**Concept Used:**

Speed (S) = Distance (D) / Time (T)

∴ Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation**:

Speed = 30 km/h

⇒ 30 / 60 km/min = 1/2 km/min

So in 30 minutes, he travels (1 / 2) × 30 = 15 km

So, the distance is 15 km

Now, in 20 minutes he has to travel 15 km

So, in 60 minutes he will travel ((15)/(20)) × 60 = 15 × 3

⇒ 45 km/h 

**His speed will be 45 km/h**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** The speed ratio is inversely proportional to the time ratio.

Given time ratio = 30 : 20

⇒ 3 : 2

So, the speed ratio will be 2 : 3

As per the question,

if the speed at 1st be 2x then increased speed = 3x

value of 2x = 30

⇒ x = 15

Then, value of 3x = 3 × 15

⇒ 45

His speed will be 45 km/h
